title: Define and Initialize a Basic Structure
description: Write a C program that defines a simple structure named `Point`. This structure should contain two integer members: `x` and `y`, representing coordinates in a 2D plane. Declare a variable of type `Point`, initialize it, and print the coordinates.
constraints: The structure `Point` must have `x` and `y` as integer members. Initialization values are fixed.
explanation: The output shows the structure's initialized values. Changing the values changes the output.

title: Accessing Structure Members with Dot Operator
description: Define a structure named `Book` with two members: `title` (a character array capable of holding a string up to 50 characters) and `pages` (an integer). In your `main` function, assign values to these members and print them.
constraints: Title string max 50 chars including null terminator. Pages must be a positive integer.
sample_output:
Book Title: The C Programming Language
Number of Pages: 272
explanation: The output displays the values assigned to the structure's members. Changing the inputs changes the output.

title: Array of Structures (Student Records)
description: Define a structure named `Student` with members `id` (an integer) and `name` (a character array up to 30 characters). Declare an array for 3 students, initialize each, and print their IDs and names.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 3 students. Student IDs are positive integers (1-100). Names are valid strings, max 30 chars.
sample_output:
Student 1: ID 101, Name Alice
Student 2: ID 102, Name Bob
Student 3: ID 103, Name Charlie
explanation: The output lists the initialized IDs and names for each student. Changing these values changes the output.

title: Accessing Structure Members via Pointers (Arrow Operator)
description: Define a structure named `Rectangle` with two floating-point members: `length` and `width`. In `main`, declare a variable of this type and a pointer to it. Assign values using the pointer and print the area.
constraints: None. The values for length and width are fixed for demonstration.
sample_output: Rectangle area after modification via pointer: 52.50
explanation: The output displays the area using the assigned values. Changing length or width changes the output.

title: Nested Structures (Person with Date of Birth)
description: Define two structures: `struct Date` (members: day, month, year) and `struct Person` (members: name and dob of type struct Date). Initialize a Person structure variable with a name and date, and print all the fields.
constraints: Name max 30 chars. Date values will form a valid date.
explanation: The output lists the input name and date of birth. Changing these values changes the output.

title: Function Returning a Structure (Complex Number Addition)
description: Define a structure named `Complex` with two floating-point members: `real` and `imag`. Write a function that takes two Complex numbers and returns their sum as a Complex value. In `main`, read two complex numbers, call the function, and print the result.
constraints: Real and imaginary parts will be floating-point numbers between -100.0 and 100.0. The sum will also fit in `float`.
explanation: The output sums the input real and imaginary parts. Changing the inputs changes the output.

title: Dynamic Array of Structures (Product Inventory)
description: Develop a C program to manage a small inventory of products. Define a structure `Product` with an `id` (integer) and `price` (float). Prompt the user to enter the number of products, then dynamically allocate memory for that many Product structures, read their details, print them, and free the memory.
constraints: The `number_of_products` `N` will be between 1 and 5. Product IDs will be integers between 1 and 100. Prices will be floating-point numbers between 0.01 and 1000.00.
sample_output:
Product Inventory:
Product ID: 101, Price: $25.50
Product ID: 102, Price: $75.00
Memory for products freed.
explanation: The output lists all product IDs and prices as entered. Changing inputs or count changes the output.

title: Employee Data Management with Function for Display
description: Define a `struct Employee` with members: `id`, `name`, and `salary`. Implement a separate function to display employee details. Initialize an array of employees and print their details using the function.
constraints: Array size fixed at 3 employees. ID: 1-999. Name: max 30 chars. Salary: 1000.00-100000.00.
sample_output:
--- Employee Details ---
Employee ID: 101, Name: Alice, Salary: $50000.00
Employee ID: 102, Name: Bob, Salary: $60000.00
Employee ID: 103, Name: Charlie, Salary: $75000.00
explanation: The output prints all initialized employee data. Changing the array values changes the output.

title: Structure Padding and `sizeof` Operator
description: Write a C program that defines a structure named `Data` with the following members in this order: `char c1; int i; char c2;`. Print the size of the structure using `sizeof`.
constraints: The structure members and their order are fixed. The size of `int` is typically 4 bytes, `char` is 1 byte, but padding can vary.
explanation: The output shows the memory size of the structure for the given member order. This can change with different compilers.

title: Library Book Inventory Management System
description: Design and implement a basic C program for a library's book inventory. Define a `struct Book` with: `title` (string, max 100 chars), `author` (string, max 50 chars), `year` (int), and `available` (int, 1 for yes and 0 for no). Prompt the user to add books, then display all books in the inventory.
constraints: The system should initially accommodate a small number of books (e.g., 2) and be able to grow using `realloc`. Max 5 books for practical testing. Titles/Authors max length as described.
sample_input:
C Programming Absolute Beginner's Guide
Greg Perry
2014
1
Data Structures and Algorithms in C
Narasimha Karumanchi
2011
0
sample_output:
--- Library Inventory ---
1. Title: C Programming Absolute Beginner's Guide, Author: Greg Perry, Year: 2014, Available: Yes
2. Title: Data Structures and Algorithms in C, Author: Narasimha Karumanchi, Year: 2011, Available: No
explanation: The output lists each book's details as entered. Different book data or count changes the output.
